summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with a history of thyroidectomy for follicular thyroid carcinoma five years earlier, hypertension, obesity and bronchial asthma, who smoked 10 cigarettes per day, presented to the emergency department with a left supraclavicular adenopathy and six days of dyspnea, asthenia, chest pain, cough and odynophagia.

Initial examination showed tachypnea at 24 breaths per minute; pulmonary auscultation found occasional wheezing and minimal bibasilar crackles, and the electrocardiogram showed sinus tachycardia. Blood tests showed hemoglobin 110 g/L, ESR 84 mm/h, GGT 79 U/L, LDH 453 U/L and CRP 7.10 mg/dL; Table 1 marks these and red blood cells, iron, TSH, T3 and alpha-1 and alpha-2 globulins as outside normal ranges, with the remaining results within normal ranges. PET-CAT showed multiple adenopathies, an anterior mediastinal mass and a significant pericardial effusion up to 25 mm.

Evacuative pericardiocentesis obtained 650 cc of serous fluid, with significant clinical improvement afterwards. Pericardial fluid analysis showed a high fluorescence population of 36.7 percent and large atypical cells with abundant mitoses; the pathological study confirmed malignant cells compatible with non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

Lymph node immunohistochemistry was positive for CD20, MUM1, BCL2 and weakly BCL6, negative for CD5, CD10, CD30 and MYC, with Ki67 80-90 percent. Bone marrow biopsy and cerebrospinal fluid showed no infiltration. The case was classified as DLBCL with a bulky mediastinal mass, non-germinal centre phenotype, stage IV-B.
She was started on R-CHOP with prophylactic rasburicase, completed all chemotherapy cycles and is currently in remission.
